scenarios.name: simulate-then-send-usdc-transfer
scenarios.rationale: Both satisfy every rubric item (simulateContract then writeContract(request), parseUnits with 6 decimals, waitForTransactionReceipt with a status === 'success' check, key from process.env via privateKeyToAccount); B adds more verification and a useful warning that the recipient is a public Hardhat test account, while A is simpler but fully correct.

scenarios.name: multicall-token-balances-with-ens
scenarios.rationale: Both normalize the name, handle a null result, and call multicall with allowFailure: false and formatUnits on the fetched decimals; B declares the ABI with parseAbi, which the rubric names explicitly, while A uses viem's built-in erc20Abi (which satisfies the "as const" intent only loosely) and also wrongly says the ENS lookup is one eth_call and the multicall is a separate call, so it describes two round trips.

scenarios.name: watch-and-query-transfer-events
scenarios.rationale: B uses watchContractEvent and getContractEvents with an ABI, a small bigint range derived from getBlockNumber, unwatch(), and the http-polling vs webSocket-push note, so it matches the rubric closely; A uses watchEvent and getLogs instead of the required functions, though it does cover unwatch, chunking and the transport note.
